headline: Maryland Governor Wes Moore called the lack of federal AI guardrails staggering and urged the nation's governors to take the lead.
score_reason: A state governor's speech reported by one local outlet, adding to a chorus of Democratic governors; no concrete measure announced.
importance_line: Marylanders and other state residents may see governors rather than Congress set AI rules, and tech firms face a patchwork of state policies, though Moore proposed no specific law and the speech date is not given.
summary: WBAL News Radio reports that Maryland Governor Wes Moore, speaking at the Maryland Innovation Summit in Baltimore, said the Trump administration's view that no federal AI legislation is needed leaves "no federal guardrails", which he called "not just concerning, it is staggering". Moore argued the administration resists controls because AI is driving the economy, saying that without it "the stock market would be down at this point", and he called on the National Governors Association to lead on the issue in Washington's absence.
notes: Follow-up of 1002:C13-09; new today is Moore's speech. Summit date not stated in the article.
